mainTopic: רבי אבין's layered questions about an אשם whose holiness moved to a new animal or changed to עולה: can a new תמורה be made with it, and must a חומש be added when it is redeemed?
overview: This amud is built around a series of questions from רבי אבין, all about an אשם whose holiness gets passed around. In the first case, a person already did תמורה with an אשם. It then got a blemish, so its holiness was moved onto a second animal. Later the owner atoned with a third animal, and the second animal became an עולה. The question is whether he can do תמורה again with that second animal. Each time, אביי objects that the case is overloaded: whichever factor bothers רבי אבין, a new animal or a new kind of holiness, could have been asked about more simply. The גמרא answers that רבי אבין is building one question on top of another (חדא מגו חדא). It gives this answer in two versions, the second based on רבי יוחנן's rule that you cannot do תמורה twice. Both versions end in תיקו. Next, רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that only a first הקדש adds a חומש when redeemed, and רב פפא shows from the פסוק that the חומש applies to the מקדיש, not the מתפיס. רבי אבין then asks the same kind of layered question about the חומש. That discussion runs through two versions, and the second continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: The end of רבי אבין's question: the replacement animal turned into an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The original אשם got a blemish and its קדושה was moved to another animal. The owner got atonement through yet another אשם, so the replacement became an עולה. Can he do תמורה with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the original אשם got a blemish, and he moved its holiness onto another animal. Then he got his atonement through a different אשם, so that second animal was switched to be an עולה. What is the law: can he do תמורה with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out רבי אבין's complicated case and asks whether a new תמורה can be done with the replacement animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner already did תמורה with the original אשם, which was mentioned just before this piece. The question is whether that earlier תמורה 'counts' against the replacement animal, which carries the same holiness passed on from the original. The twist is that the replacement is now an עולה, so its holiness has changed type.

keyTerms.meaning: it became blemished, so it can no longer be brought as a קרבן
he redeemed it by moving its holiness onto another animal
a guilt offering
it was switched over to be brought as a burnt offering
to substitute: declaring a regular animal as a replacement for a holy one, which makes both holy

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The beginning of רבי אבין's question, where the owner already did תמורה with the first אשם, came just before. Keep in mind that one תמורה has already happened.

phrases.english: and it became blemished, and he redeemed it onto another animal,
and he achieved atonement with a different guilt offering,
and it (the second animal) was switched to be a burnt offering —
what is the law — may he substitute for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ שֶׁיָּמִיר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבין's question, which began before this piece.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can תמורה be done with a replacement animal that now has a new body and a new type of holiness, when the original holiness was already used for תמורה once?

steps.title: אביי: if two animals is the issue, why add the atonement detail?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what is really bothering רבי אבין. If the issue is two bodies with one holiness, he could have asked without the owner getting atonement elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What exactly is his question? If it is about two bodies sharing one holiness, let him ask it even where the owner did not get atonement through another animal.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges how the question is built. If the concern is only that a new animal is involved, the extra detail about the animal becoming an עולה is unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the holiness from the blemished animal to a new one creates 'two bodies, one holiness,' since both are still אשם. If that alone is the doubt, רבי אבין should have stopped there. Adding the atonement and the change to עולה seems like extra baggage.

keyTerms.meaning: two bodies, meaning two different animals
one and the same type of holiness
let him ask it (in a simpler case)
achieving atonement

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: אביי said: What is it that he is asking?
If it is about two bodies and one holiness —
let him ask it even without the atonement.
phrases.notes: Meaning: in a case where the second animal simply stays an אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the structure of רבי אבין's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra detail in רבי אבין's case that the owner got atonement elsewhere and the animal became an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the doubt comes from having a new animal, that doubt already exists before any atonement, so the extra detail is pointless.

steps.title: אביי: if two holinesses is the issue, why add the blemish detail?
steps.stepSummary: The second half of אביי's challenge: if the issue is a change in the type of holiness, he could have asked without the blemish and the transfer to a new animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is about two holinesses in one body, let him ask it even where the animal never got a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his challenge from the other side. If the concern is the change from אשם to עולה, that could happen to the original animal itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a blemish, the original animal could get lost, the owner could atone with another, and the original would become an עולה. That is 'one body, two holinesses.' So the blemish and the transfer also seem unnecessary. Either way, רבי אבין's case looks overloaded.

keyTerms.meaning: two types of holiness (first אשם, then עולה)
one body, the same animal

phrases.english: If it is about two holinesses and one body —
let him ask it even without the blemish!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת, וְגוּף אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's two-sided challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The blemish and transfer detail in רבי אבין's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the doubt comes from the change in holiness, that can happen without a new animal, so the blemish detail is pointless.

steps.title: רבי אבין is asking one question built on another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אבין's case is two questions stacked together. Even if two animals with the same holiness cannot get a new תמורה, maybe two animals with two different holinesses can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין is asking one question that grows out of another. If you conclude that with two bodies and one holiness he cannot substitute again, because that holiness was already substituted once, then what about two bodies and two holinesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבין. The complicated case is on purpose: it is a follow-up question that only arises once you assume an answer to the simpler one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step one: two bodies, one holiness. We might rule that no new תמורה works, because this same holiness was already used for a תמורה. Step two: if that is the reason, maybe when the holiness itself changes to עולה it counts as 'new,' and a new תמורה would work. That is why רבי אבין needed both the blemish and the atonement in his case.

keyTerms.meaning: one question that comes out of another
if you end up saying (if you resolve the first question this way)
one time

steps.confusionAlert: The word אִיתְּמַר here does not mean 'it was said,' as it usually does. It comes from תמורה and means 'it was substituted.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern: a question that looks overloaded is really a second-level question that depends on assuming an answer to the first.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And רבי אבין is asking one question out of another,
and if you conclude:
two bodies and one holiness — no (he cannot substitute),
because with that very holiness
a substitution was already made one time.
phrases.notes: The word אִיתְּמַר comes from להמיר, so it means 'it was substituted,' not 'it was said.'

phrases.english: two bodies and two holinesses — what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by explaining that the case is built in two layers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restructuring the question as a follow-up question (אם תימצי לומר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed רבי אבין had a single doubt, so the extra details looked unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אבין first assumes two bodies with one holiness cannot get a new תמורה, then asks whether a change in holiness makes it work.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question stands without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle רבי אבין's follow-up question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether a change from אשם to עולה makes the holiness 'new' enough for another תמורה. The doubt remains.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבין's question has two layers. First, suppose two animals with one holiness cannot get a second תמורה, because that holiness was already substituted once. Second, if so, when the holiness changes type (אשם to עולה), maybe a new תמורה works. The second question is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the reformulated question from step 4 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a new תמורה can be done with two bodies that have two different holinesses remains undecided.

steps.title: Second version: same holiness, new animal
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, רבי אבין asks according to רבי יוחנן. An אשם already had one תמורה made with it, then got a blemish, and its holiness moved to another animal. Can a new תמורה be made with that new animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: רבי אבין asked according to רבי יוחנן, who holds you cannot make a תמורה and then make another one. Someone set aside an אשם and made a תמורה with it. Then it got a blemish, and he moved its holiness onto another animal. Can he now make a תמורה again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of רבי אבין's question. This first case is about a new animal carrying the very same holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that one animal can only cause a תמורה once. Here a תמורה was already made, but now the holiness sits in a different body. So the question is whether the 'once only' rule follows the holiness or the physical animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a second way the discussion was passed down
You cannot make a תמורה and then go back and make another one
It got a blemish, so it can no longer be brought as a קרבן
He took away its holiness by moving it onto something else

steps.confusionAlert: In this version the case says 'וְהֵמִיר בּוֹ': a תמורה was already made once. That is why רבי יוחנן's 'only once' rule matters here.

phrases.english: Another version:
Rabbi Avin asked according to Rabbi Yochanan,
who said one cannot substitute and then go back and substitute again:
if he set aside a guilt offering to gain atonement with it,
and he substituted for it,
and it became blemished and he moved its holiness onto another animal,
may he go back and substitute again?

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, בָּעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the whole discussion (Steps 1-5) as a second version, now built on רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the 'only one תמורה' rule carry over to a new animal that holds the same holiness?

steps.title: Second case: same animal, new kind of holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין adds a second case. The owner got atonement through a different אשם, so this animal became an עולה. Can a new תמורה be made with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he got atonement through another אשם, and this animal was moved over to become an עולה, can he go back and make a תמורה again?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין asks a second case that is the mirror image of the first. Here the animal stays the same, but its holiness changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the body changed and the holiness stayed the same. Here the body stays the same and the holiness changes from אשם to עולה. Together the two cases test both sides of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: He already got atonement (through a different קרבן)
It was moved over to become an עולה

phrases.english: If he got atonement through another guilt offering,
and this one was moved over to be a burnt offering,
may he go back and substitute again?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר, וְנִיתַּק זֶה לְעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the question in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the 'only one תמורה' rule still apply when the same animal takes on a different kind of holiness?

steps.title: אביי: if the issue is a new holiness, why ask the blemish case?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks which issue is really bothering רבי אבין. If the issue is a new holiness in the same body, the blemish case does not test that at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Which one is he really asking about? If he is asking about a different holiness in the same body, he should not ask about the case where it got a blemish and was moved to another animal!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי אבין for asking two questions. This is the first half of his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blemish case is about a new body with the same holiness. So if רבי אבין's real doubt is about a new holiness in the same body, the blemish case does not belong in his question.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one is he really asking about?
A different kind of holiness in the same animal

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Which one is he really asking about?
If it is a different holiness in the same body,
he should not ask about it becoming blemished and being moved onto another!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֵי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why רבי אבין asked two separate cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's choice to include the blemish case (Step 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The blemish case tests a new body, not a new holiness, so it is not needed if the doubt is about holiness.

steps.title: אביי: if the issue is a new body, why ask the atonement case?
steps.stepSummary: This is the second half of אביי's challenge. If the issue is a new body with the same holiness, the atonement case does not test that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is asking about another body with the same holiness, he should not ask about the case where the owner got atonement through another אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his challenge from the other side. Either way, one of רבי אבין's two cases seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The atonement case keeps the same body and changes the holiness. So it cannot test whether a new body matters. Taken together, the two halves say each case only fits one possible doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A different animal with the same holiness

phrases.english: If it is another body with the same holiness,
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'אֶחָד' (one), in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is 'אַחֵר' (another).

phrases.english: he should not ask about gaining atonement through another guilt offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי גּוּף אַחֵר בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge begun in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's choice to include the atonement case (Step 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The atonement case tests a new holiness, not a new body, so it is not needed if the doubt is about the body.

steps.title: Answer: רבי אבין builds one question on top of the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אבין asks one question that grows out of the other. It starts by restating the first question, the blemish case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבין is asking one question out of the other: if the animal got a blemish and he moved its holiness onto another animal, can he go back and make a תמורה again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבין by saying the two cases are linked, not repeated. It begins by restating the first question so it can explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין is not asking two separate questions. He asks the blemish case first, and the second case only comes up depending on how the first one is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: One question growing out of the other

phrases.english: And Rabbi Avin:

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: he is asking one question out of the other:
if it became blemished and he moved its holiness onto another animal,
may he go back and substitute again?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the two cases form one step-by-step question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבין asked two unrelated questions, and one of them was not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second case only arises after a possible answer to the first, so both are needed.

steps.title: The two sides of the first question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out the two possible sides of the blemish case. Maybe only the original אשם is limited to one תמורה. Or maybe anything holding that same holiness is limited.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that only the first אשם cannot have a second תמורה, but another animal, even though it holds the same holiness, can have a new תמורה? Or perhaps anything with that same holiness cannot have another תמורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what רבי אבין is unsure about in the first case: does the 'only once' rule follow the animal or the holiness?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the rule belongs to the physical animal, so a new animal starts fresh. Side two: the rule belongs to the holiness, so any animal carrying it stays limited. The second case (the עולה) is the next question that would follow if the answer is side two.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say?
Or perhaps
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, רבי אבין's question is a ladder. First: does the 'only one תמורה' rule follow the holiness to a new animal? If it does, the next question is whether a different holiness in the same animal starts fresh.

phrases.english: Do we say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאָשָׁם רִאשׁוֹן הוּא דְּאֵין חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר,
phrases.english: it is only with the first guilt offering that he cannot substitute again,
but with another body,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקַדִּישׁ אוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה —
phrases.english: even though it is holy with that same holiness,
he may substitute again;
or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה אֵין חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר?
phrases.english: anything with that same holiness cannot be substituted again?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן: בְּאָשָׁם רִאשׁוֹן הוּא דְּאֵין חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the first question that Step 10 restated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the 'only one תמורה' limit tied to the original animal, or to the holiness wherever it goes?

steps.title: The second question: same animal, new holiness
steps.stepSummary: Suppose a new animal carrying the same holiness cannot be used for another תמורה. Then what about the original אשם after it has become an עולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you conclude that this other animal cannot be used for a new תמורה, since it holds the same holiness, then ask this: the owner got atonement through a different אשם, and this first animal was moved to become an עולה. Can he now make a new תמורה with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks רבי אבין's second question, which only comes up if the first question is answered strictly. The case is an אשם that turned into an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question was about a new body holding the same holiness (the blemish case). This question flips it: the body is the same, but the holiness is new, because the animal is now an עולה. Step 10 explained that this is how the two questions grow out of each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you conclude. Used to build a second question on one possible answer to the first.
A different body, meaning a different animal
Got atonement
Was moved over to become an עולה

phrases.english: And if you conclude
that this other body,
phrases.notes: Again, read "another" (square brackets), not "one" (round brackets). It means the replacement animal from the blemish case.

phrases.english: since it stands in the same holiness,
one cannot go back and make a substitute with it
then what if he got atonement through another אשם
and this first animal was moved over to be an עולה
what is the law: may he again make a substitute with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצָא לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a second question on the strict answer to the first question from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a new תמורה be made with the same animal once its holiness has changed from אשם to עולה?

steps.title: Two sides of the second question, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the limit applies only to the same body with the same holiness. Or maybe the same body is limited no matter what holiness it has. The question stays open (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that the rule 'one cannot make a substitute and then make another substitute' only applies to the same animal with the same holiness, but the same animal with a different holiness can be used again? Or maybe even with a different holiness, since it is the same animal, it cannot be used again? The question stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible ways to look at the second question. It does not decide between them and ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: what counts is the holiness, so a new holiness allows a new תמורה. Side two: what counts is the body, so the same animal stays limited even with new holiness. No answer is found, so the question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only to... (limits a rule to a certain case)
Or perhaps. Introduces the other side of a question.
A different kind of holiness
Let it stand. The question is left unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבין's two questions test what limits a תמורה: the holiness or the animal's body. The second question, same body with new holiness, ends in תיקו.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no' or 'yes.' It means the גמרא could not decide, so the question stays open.

phrases.english: Do we say
that when we say one cannot make a substitute and then make another,

but the same body in a different holiness
may be used again to make a substitute?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question asked in step 12 and closes it with תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the limit on a second תמורה follow the body or the holiness?

steps.title: Only the first הקדש adds a fifth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that redeeming a first הקדש requires adding a חומש, but redeeming a second הקדש does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: a first consecrated item adds a fifth when redeemed, but a second consecrated item does not add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching with a similar idea of first versus second holiness. It is about the extra fifth, the חומש, paid when redeeming הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an owner who redeems his own הקדש pays its value plus a חומש. רבי יהושע בן לוי says this applies only to the original הקדש. An animal that became holy second, in place of a blemished offering that was redeemed, is redeemed without the חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, original consecrated item
A second consecrated item that took over holiness from an earlier one
Adds a fifth on top of the value when redeeming

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a second holiness can have weaker rules than a first holiness. That idea connects to רבי אבין's questions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A first consecrated item adds a fifth,
but a second consecrated item does not add a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related teaching after רבי אבין's questions end in תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חומש is added only when redeeming a first הקדש, not a second one.

steps.title: The source: the one who consecrates, not the one who transfers
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the פסוק requires the חומש from the מקדיש, the one who consecrates directly, and not from the מתפיס, who transfers holiness from another item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What is the reason of רבי יהושע בן לוי? The verse says: 'And if he who consecrates will redeem his house, he shall add a fifth.' This means the one who consecrates, and not the one who transfers holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks for the source of רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule and answers right away with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word מקדיש, someone who makes a thing holy on his own. A second הקדש gets its holiness from an earlier holy item, so its owner is a מתפיס rather than a מקדיש. That is why he does not add the חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
One who makes something holy directly
One who transfers holiness from another item onto this one
Will redeem

steps.whatToRemember: חומש is paid only by the מקדיש. A second הקדש comes from a מתפיס, so no חומש is added.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?
The verse says:
"And if he who consecrates will redeem his house,
then he shall add a fifth"
the one who consecrates, and not the one who transfers holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in a פסוק for the rule stated in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that a second הקדש does not add a חומש
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 27:15, which uses the word המקדיש, read as excluding the מתפיס

steps.title: רבי אבין's question about a replacement animal that became an עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין asks: a blemished אשם was redeemed with a חומש onto a second animal. The owner atoned with a third animal, so the second animal was moved to be an עולה. Must a חומש be added when redeeming it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין asked: Someone set aside an אשם, it got a blemish, he added a fifth and redeemed it onto another animal. Then he atoned with yet another אשם, and this second animal was moved to be an עולה. Does he need to add a fifth for it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין asks a detailed question: does a second animal that got its holiness from an earlier אשם, and then became an עולה, need a חומש when it is redeemed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a second הקדש does not get a חומש. The second animal here took its holiness from the first one, so normally it would not need one. But now its holiness has changed to עולה, so maybe it counts as a fresh, first holiness that does need a חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering
It became blemished and can no longer be offered
The extra fifth added when redeeming consecrated property
He redeemed it, moving its holiness onto something else
It was moved over to become an עולה

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin asked:
If one set aside a guilt offering to gain atonement with it,
and it became blemished, and he added a fifth to it,
and redeemed it onto another animal,
and he gained atonement with yet another guilt offering,
and this one was moved to be a burnt offering —
phrases.notes: "This one" is the second animal, the one that got the holiness from the blemished אשם.

phrases.english: must he add a fifth on it when it is redeemed?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule that a second הקדש has no חומש to a case where the holiness later changed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a second animal whose holiness changed from אשם to עולה require a חומש on redemption?

steps.title: אביי: if the issue is two bodies, why mention the atonement?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what exactly רבי אבין is unsure about. If it is about a second animal with the same holiness, the atonement and the move to עולה are unneeded details.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What is he really asking? If he is asking about two animals with one holiness, he could ask it even without the owner atoning with another animal.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts challenging the question by saying it has extra details that don't seem needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doubt is only whether a second animal carrying the same אשם holiness needs a חומש, then the case could stop before the third animal and the switch to עולה. Adding those details makes no sense for that question.

keyTerms.meaning: Two bodies, meaning two different animals
One and the same kind of holiness
Let him ask it (in a simpler case)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Abaye said: What is he asking about?
If it is two bodies and one holiness
that he is asking about —
let him ask it even where he did not gain atonement!
phrases.notes: Meaning: leave out the third animal and the switch to עולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the structure of רבי אבין's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra details in רבי אבין's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the doubt is two bodies with one holiness, the atonement and the switch to עולה are unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: if the issue is two holinesses, why mention the blemish?
steps.stepSummary: אביי continues: if the question is about one animal that holds two holinesses, the blemish and the redemption onto a second animal are unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is asking about two holinesses on one animal, he could ask it even where the first animal never got a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his challenge by pointing out the second side: the blemish detail also seems unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doubt is whether changing holiness from אשם to עולה makes a fresh holiness, you could ask it about the original אשם itself becoming an עולה. There would be no need for a blemish or a second animal. So neither reading explains the full case.

keyTerms.meaning: Two different kinds of holiness
One body, meaning the same animal

phrases.english: If it is two holinesses and one body
that he is asking about —
let him ask it even where it was not blemished!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת, וְגוּף אֶחָד קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of אביי's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The blemish detail in רבי אבין's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the doubt is one body with two holinesses, the blemish and the second animal are unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי אבין builds one question on top of another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רבי אבין is asking a follow-up question. Even if two bodies with one holiness get no חומש, what about two bodies with two holinesses?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין is asking one question that grows out of another: If you say that two animals with one holiness don't need a fifth because a fifth was already added once for that holiness, what about two animals with two holinesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבין and explains why every detail in his case is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe a second animal with the same holiness gets no חומש because a חומש was already paid for that holiness. Here the second animal now has a new holiness (עולה), which never had a חומש paid. So the full case is needed to ask about two bodies and two holinesses together.

keyTerms.meaning: One question out of another, a follow-up question
If you decide that... (assume one answer and ask further)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אבין is asking about just one issue. He first assumes an answer to the simpler question, and then asks a harder one on top of it.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Avin is asking one question out of another:
If you will say
that two bodies with one holiness do not need a fifth —
because with that holiness
a fifth was already added one time,
what about two bodies and two holinesses?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by showing why all details are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the question as a layered follow-up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the case had unnecessary details.
steps.terutzMaskana: The details create a case of two bodies and two holinesses, a new question built on the simpler one.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבי אבין's question without an answer: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion with no answer to רבי אבין's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know whether a new holiness on a second animal brings back the חומש. The question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A second animal with the same holiness gets no חומש, possibly because a חומש was already paid for that holiness. Whether a second animal with a new holiness needs a חומש is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי אבין's question without a ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of two bodies and two holinesses remains an open question regarding חומש.

steps.title: Another version of רבי אבין's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי אבין's question: does a second animal that replaced a blemished אשם, and was later moved to be an עולה, need a חומש when it is redeemed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: רבי אבין asked: Someone set aside an אשם to atone with it. It became blemished, and he redeemed it onto another animal and added a fifth. Then they atoned with a different אשם, and this animal was moved to be an עולה. Must he add a fifth when he redeems it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אבין's question again, the way another tradition reported it. This sets up a second round of אביי's challenge and the גמרא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three animals: the first אשם, which got a blemish; the second animal, which got the first one's holiness through redemption with a חומש; and a third animal that was actually used for atonement. Because the owner already atoned, the second animal is moved to be an עולה. The question is whether redeeming this second animal needs a חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a second way the discussion was reported
Guilt offering
It became blemished, so it can no longer be brought as a קרבן
He redeemed it, moving its holiness onto another animal
An added fifth, paid by the owner when he redeems his own consecrated item
It was moved to be an עולה (burnt offering)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the three animals separate. The question is about the SECOND animal, the one that got its holiness through redemption and was later moved to be an עולה.

phrases.english: Another version:
Rabbi Avin asked:
If one set aside a guilt offering to atone with it,
and it became blemished, and he redeemed it onto another animal
and added a fifth,
and they atoned with a different guilt offering,
and this one was moved to be a burnt offering,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the second animal, the one that got the first animal's holiness.

phrases.english: what is the law: must he add a fifth on it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לישנא אחרינא, בעי רבי אבין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the question that was left as תיקו in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether redeeming the second animal, which got its holiness through redemption and was then moved to be an עולה, needs a חומש.

steps.title: אביי asks which question רבי אבין really means
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the question: if it is about a new holiness in the same body, the blemish detail is unneeded; if it is about another body with the same holiness, the other details are unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Which one is he asking about? If he is asking about a different holiness in the same body, he should not mention "it became blemished." If he is asking about another body with the same holiness, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says the question has too many details. Each possible point of doubt makes some of the details unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doubt is about one animal that changed from אשם to עולה, the blemish and redemption onto a second animal add nothing. If the doubt is about a second animal that kept the same holiness, the atonement with a third animal and the move to עולה add nothing. The word כו׳ is short for that second half, which we already saw in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: A different holiness in the same body: the same animal changing from one קרבן type to another
Another body with the same holiness: a new animal carrying the original holiness
He should not need to ask about (this detail)
"Etc.": the rest is as said before

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Which one is he asking about?
If it is a different holiness in the same body
that he is asking about,
he should not ask about "it became blemished";
if it is another body with the same holiness, etc.
phrases.notes: Read "another" (square brackets) instead of "one" (round brackets). The "etc." means the atonement and the move to עולה are not needed, as in step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי: הדין קא מיבעיא ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the extra details in the question from step 21, just as in steps 17 and 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The many details in רבי אבין's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each possible point of doubt makes part of the case unnecessary, so the question does not seem to hold together.

steps.title: Laying out the first stage: a second animal with the same holiness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain the question in stages. First stage: the blemished אשם was redeemed onto another animal. Maybe a חומש is added only for the first אשם and not for another body, even though it has the same holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He redeemed it onto another animal: must he add a fifth when redeeming that one? Do we say: it is only for the first אשם that he adds a fifth, but for another body, even though it has the same holiness, he does not add a fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by showing that the question is built in stages. It starts with the simpler question about a second animal that still has the same אשם holiness. This passage ends in the middle of that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first stage asks whether a חומש applies to an animal that is a new body but carries the same holiness. One side says a חומש belongs only to the original אשם, so the second animal would need none. Each detail of רבי אבין's case will turn out to belong to a different stage of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say? This introduces one side of a doubt
The first אשם: the animal the owner originally set aside
Even though
It stands, meaning it remains in that state

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first stage of the question, not the final ruling. The sentence continues past the end of this passage.

phrases.english: And he redeemed it onto another animal:
must he add a fifth on it?
Do we say:
it is for the first guilt offering that he adds,
but for another body,
phrases.notes: Again, read "another" (square brackets) instead of "one" (round brackets).

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָאֵים בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: even though it has the same holiness,
he does not add a fifth,
phrases.notes: The word "not" is in square brackets, so it belongs in the corrected wording. The thought continues after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וחללו על אחר, מהו שיוסיף עליו חומש? מי אמרינן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 22 by laying out the question in stages, starting with the first stage.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Step-by-step question: one question builds on the expected answer to an earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the question had unneeded details, because it seemed to be one single question.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question has stages. The first stage is about another body with the same holiness, so the blemish and redemption details are needed for that stage.
